chunkAll.title: POST /user/{userId}/freeze — Freeze User
chunkAll.text:
POST /user/{userId}/freeze

Freeze User

Freeze a user you provisioned. A partner pays for its active users, so freezing a user
it no longer pays for suspends that user. The user's monetary accounts and cards are frozen
along with the user, while the user's subscription and partner connection are kept intact so
the user can be unfrozen later. The partner keeps access to the frozen user.

Send an empty request body. Reopen the user later with the unfreeze endpoint.

Path parameters: userId.

Responses:
- 200: User frozen successfully

chunkAll.title: POST /user/{userId}/unfreeze — Unfreeze User
chunkAll.text:
POST /user/{userId}/unfreeze

Unfreeze User

Unfreeze a user you previously froze. The user's monetary accounts and cards are unfrozen
along with the user and returned to active. Use this when the partner resumes paying for the
user.

Send an empty request body.

Path parameters: userId.

Responses:
- 200: User unfrozen successfully

chunkAll.title: POST /user/{userId}/attachment — Upload attachment
chunkAll.text:
POST /user/{userId}/attachment

Upload attachment

Upload a file attachment for the provisioned user. The resulting attachment ID can then be
passed to `PUT /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry/{inquiryId}/partner-user-information-inquiry-entry/{entryId}`
via `all_attachment_id` to submit documents for an inquiry entry.

The request body is the **raw binary content** of the file. The content type and an
optional description are passed as headers, not in the body.

**Supported content types:** `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `application/pdf`

Path parameters: userId.

Responses:
- 200: Attachment uploaded successfully. Returns the ID to use in inquiry entry submissions.
- 400: Bad request — unsupported content type or missing body.

chunkAll.title: PUT /user/{userId}/challenge-request/{challengeRequestId} — Update Challenge Request
chunkAll.text:
PUT /user/{userId}/challenge-request/{challengeRequestId}

Update Challenge Request

Accept or reject a Mastercard Identity Check (3DS) challenge request.

When accepting, you may optionally pass `monetary_account_id` to choose which account
the follow-up transaction is charged from. When omitted, the account is determined
automatically: by savings auto-route if the user has it enabled, otherwise the card's
primary account.

On acceptance the available balance of the selected account (or the automatically
determined one) is checked against the transaction amount. If it is insufficient the
approval is rejected with a `400` and the challenge request keeps its current status,
so it can be retried against a different account.

Path parameters: userId, challengeRequestId.

Request fields:
- status: The status of the identity check.
- monetary_account_id: The monetary account the transaction should be charged from. Optional, and
only meaningful when accepting. When omitted the account is determined
automatically.


Responses:
- 200: Challenge request updated successfully
- 400: The selected account — or, when none was selected, the automatically determined
one — does not have enough money to complete the payment. The challenge request
status is left unchanged.

chunkAll.text:
POST /user/{userId}/notification-filter-url

Create/Update/Delete Notification Filter URLs

Create, update, or delete webhook endpoints to receive notifications for specific events.

**Important Notes:**
- This endpoint completely **replaces** all existing notification filters for the user
- To **add** notifications: Include all existing + new filters in the request
- To **update** notifications: Include all filters with updated settings  
- To **delete all** notifications: Send empty array `{}`
- To **add** notifications for the UserProvisions -> create a session for the user, and use the UserApiKey.id as the "userId" in the request URL

**Examples:**
- Current: 3 notification types configured
- To add 1 more: Send POST with all 4 types (3 existing + 1 new)
- To remove 1: Send POST with 2 types (excluding the unwanted one)
- To clear all: Send POST with `{"notification_filters": []}`

Path parameters: userId.

Request fields:
- notification_filters: Array of notification filters to create

Responses:
- 200: Notification filter URLs created successfully
- 400: Bad request - invalid URL or category

chunkAll.title: GET /user/{userId}/notification-filter-failure — List Notification Filter Failures
chunkAll.text:
GET /user/{userId}/notification-filter-failure

List Notification Filter Failures

Retrieve all notification filter failures that have occurred when trying to deliver webhooks
for the given user.

The notifications of the underlying users of the partner are linked with the partner's company
user. The `userId` should be the `UserCompany.id` of the partner — the response will include
failed notifications for all underlying provisioned users.

**Response includes:**
- Failed notification details
- Error descriptions and timestamps
- Response code from the webhook endpoint (or null)
- Associated notification filter configuration

Path parameters: userId.

Responses:
- 200: List of notification filter failures

chunkAll.title: POST /user/{userId}/notification-filter-failure — Retry Failed Notification Deliveries
chunkAll.text:
POST /user/{userId}/notification-filter-failure

Retry Failed Notification Deliveries

Retry delivery of failed webhook notifications by specifying their failure IDs.

**Key Features:**
- Retry up to 100 failed notifications in a single request
- Multiple IDs can be provided as comma-separated values
- Only failed notifications belonging to the specified user can be retried
- Successfully queued retries will return the failure IDs that were processed

**Use Cases:**
- Retry notifications after fixing webhook endpoint issues
- Bulk retry of failures after maintenance windows
- Recovery from temporary network or service outages

Path parameters: userId.

Request fields:
- notification_filter_failed_ids: Comma-separated list of notification filter failure IDs to retry.
Maximum of 100 IDs allowed per request.


Responses:
- 200: Retry successfully queued. Returns an empty response body.
- 400: Bad request - invalid IDs, too many IDs, or malformed request
- 404: Not found - one or more failure IDs don't exist or don't belong to the user

chunkAll.title: GET /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry — List User Information Inquiries
chunkAll.text:
GET /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry

List User Information Inquiries

Returns all `UserInformationInquiry` objects for the given provisioned user.

Partners have **read-only** access to inquiries. Inquiries are created internally by bunq
based on compliance or onboarding triggers — partners cannot create or update them.

**Merging behavior**: When multiple inquiries are created for the same user under the same
context, bunq merges them into a single inquiry and appends new entries to it.

**Polling recommendation**: Use `status=EXPECTING_REPLY_FROM_USER` to find open inquiries
that still require user action.

Path parameters: userId.

Responses:
- 200: List of user information inquiries
- 400: Bad request - invalid parameters

chunkAll.title: PUT /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry/{inquiryId}/partner-user-information-inquiry-entry/{entryId} — Submit answer for inquiry entry
chunkAll.text:
PUT /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry/{inquiryId}/partner-user-information-inquiry-entry/{entryId}

Submit answer for inquiry entry

Submit an answer for a specific `UserInformationInquiryEntry` on behalf of the provisioned
user. This is how partners provide the information bunq has requested.

Each entry can be answered with either:
- **Attachments** (`all_attachment_id`): for document-based entries (e.g. ID verification,
  bank statements). Upload the files first via `POST /user/{userId}/attachment`, then
  pass the resulting attachment IDs here.
- **Free text** (`answer`): for open-ended questions (e.g. source of income, account
  purpose). Both fields are optional but at least one must be provided.

After a successful PUT the entry status transitions to `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW`. Once all
entries in the inquiry are in `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW`, the inquiry status moves to
`EXPECTING_REPLY_FROM_BUNQ`.

**Constraints:**
- Only entries with status `PENDING` can be updated. Submitting against a non-pending
  entry (e.g. `CANCELLED`, `APPROVED`) returns HTTP 400.
- Attachments must belong to the provisioned user. Passing an attachment owned by a
  different user returns HTTP 400.

Path parameters: userId, inquiryId, entryId.

Request fields:
- all_attachment_id: IDs of attachments to submit for this entry. Upload files first via
`POST /user/{userId}/attachment`. Use for document-based entries.

- answer: Free-text answer for open-ended entries (e.g. source of income,
account purpose, involvement in politics).


Responses:
- 200: Entry submitted successfully. Returns the ID of the updated entry.
- 400: Bad request. Possible causes:
- Entry is not in `PENDING` status
- One or more attachment IDs belong to a different user

chunkAll.title: GET /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry/{inquiryId} — Get User Information Inquiry
chunkAll.text:
GET /user/{userId}/user-information-inquiry/{inquiryId}

Get User Information Inquiry

Returns the full `UserInformationInquiry` object for the given inquiry ID, including
all entries and their current status.

Path parameters: userId, inquiryId.

Responses:
- 200: User information inquiry details
- 404: Inquiry not found

chunkAll.title: KYC and identity verification — Overview
chunkAll.text:
Overview

KYC means Know Your Customer. Before a provisioned user can hold money or make
payments, the user must pass identity verification. The partner starts the
verification, the user gives identity data and a document, and bunq reviews it.

chunkAll.title: KYC and identity verification — Steps
chunkAll.text:
Steps

1. Start the verification for the user.
2. Collect the user identity data: name, address, nationality, tax residence.
3. Upload an identity document, then link it to the verification.
4. Submit the verification for review.
5. Poll the verification status until it is approved or rejected.

chunkAll.title: KYC and identity verification — Status values
chunkAll.text:
Status values

- PENDING: the verification is started but not submitted.
- SUBMITTED: bunq is reviewing the data.
- APPROVED: the user passed and can use the account.
- REJECTED: the user did not pass. Read the reason and retry.
